title: Choir and Harvest
premise: Juniper Nystrom returns to the family orchard to bury their twin brother, Alder, only to discover the mirrors lagging a second behind reality — and in that stolen second, something wearing Alder's face is learning to move. The Nystroms, it turns out, were one of four founding families bound to a harvest ritual that trades a twin's life for the town's abundance, and this year's debt has come due. Juniper must choose between completing the ritual and becoming what their ancestors were: keepers of a lie fed on borrowed time. In the end, Juniper breaks the circle by giving the harvest back its own name, shattering every mirror in the house and letting the town's prosperity rot with the truth.
about_author: Cyrus Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing estate sales in rural farming towns, where he collected more family secrets than furniture. He writes horror about inheritance — the kind you can't sell, burn, or refuse.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Arriving home for Alder's funeral, Juniper notices small wrongnesses: the coffin is sealed early, their mother won't look at them, and the house's mirrors show rooms a heartbeat behind. The emotional beat is grief curdling into suspicion as Juniper realizes the town treats the funeral less like mourning and more like a payment received.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with interludes from the mirror-Alder. Testing the lag deliberately, Juniper watches their reflection hesitate before matching them — then stop matching at all. A founder's ledger in the attic reveals the twin-harvest pact and that Alder was buried alive by choice. The beat is dread deepening into complicity: Juniper understands they were always the backup.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The other founding families arrive for the equinox, polite and merciless, insisting the ritual must finish or the town starves as it did once before. Mirror-Alder pleads through the glass, claiming he can still be saved if Juniper takes his place willingly. The beat is moral collapse: Juniper, exhausted and grieving, almost says yes.

chapters.title: Give It Back Its Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climaxing at the ritual circle beneath the orchard. Instead of completing the rite or substituting themselves, Juniper speaks the harvest's true name aloud — the thing the founders enslaved — and offers it freedom instead of tribute. The mirrors shatter; Alder dies truly, at peace; the fields go fallow but honest. The beat is costly release: inheritance refused, memory kept.
